header.name: Communications Networking - An analytical approach
header.description: The course introduces the student to analytical tools that help analyze a communications network. We will learn to apply simple queueing models to analyze the delay, throughput, and timeliness performance of networks. We will analyze randomized multiaccess and scheduling. We will study and compare congestion control algorithms for optimizing the utilities like throughput and age of information over an end-to-end path.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to apply queueing models to analyze the metrics of throughput, delay, and age of information.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to analyze common randomized multiaccess and network scheduling algorithms

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to explain, compare and contrast flow and congestion control algorithms of the transmission control protocol.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The student will be able to use simulations and real world experiments to reproduce network behaviors of interest

lecture_topics: Applications and their requirements (in terms of common metrics of throughput, delay, and age of information)
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Students handpick a few protocols at each layer and discuss their functionalities. List the queues in the protocol stack.

lecture_topics: Review of Discrete Time Markov Chains
Delay, throughput and age analysis for queues (Little’s theorem, M/M/* queues, M/G/1, networks of queues)
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Word problems, paper readings, and simulations of queues, delay, throughput, and age measurements in a real setting

lecture_topics: Throughput analysis of ALOHA and CSMA
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Word problems, ns3 simulations/ WiFi experiments

lecture_topics: TCP Congestion and Flow Control Algorithms (loss-based, delay-based, and hybrid)
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Paper Reading and Real-world experiments that bring forth the salient features of the algorithms

Communication Networks By R. Srikant and Lei Ying
